newsitem.title: CHINA: NEW WORLD TELEPHONE LAUNCHES PCS PHONE NETWORK.
newsitem.headline: NEW WORLD TELEPHONE LAUNCHES PCS PHONE NETWORK.

text.p: New World Telephone Group announced the launch of a new mobile service on Thursday and said it would invest HK$5.0 billion in developing the network over the next three years.

New World Telephone, a subsidiary of New World Development Co Ltd, said it had already invested almost HK$3.0 billion in the PCS 009 mobile telephone service and expected to have more than 100,000 subscribers by the end of June 1998.

"New World Telephone shareholders are committed to making long term investment in this network infrastructure... We plan to spend over HK$5.0 billion in the next three years," New World Telephone technical director Albert Wong told a news conference.

New World Telephone chief executive Peter Tsang said the company expected to break even within five to seven years and the total number of customers in Hong Kong could reach as high as two to four million people.
"New World Telephone understands that telecommunications services are a long term investment," he said.
The network currently has 250 operational cell sites and was expected to expand to 300 sites by the end of September and 500 sites by mid-1998, providing blanket coverage of Hong Kong, Wong said.

New World Telephone said it planned to provide roaming services next year in 70 countries, including Hong Kong's major trading partners in South East Asia and Europe, many of which already had PCS networks.
"I anticipate that in the next two months we will have the first few roaming country services," Wong said.
Roaming services would also be provided in mainland China in the next month or so through handset-roaming until China built a PCS network, commercial director Franky Lai said.
New World Telephone provides telecommunications services including fixed, mobile, PCS (personal communication service) and multimedia services to individuals and corporations.
